settings.description: A home brew guide from Little Ember, a small-batch coffee roaster.

settings.title: Choose your brewer
settings.description: Measure coffee and water by weight. Start with one recipe and keep a note of what you change.

tabs.title: Pour-over
tabs.subtitle: 20 g coffee / 320 g water
tabs.content: Rinse the paper filter and add medium-ground coffee. Wet the grounds with about 45 g of water. Wait 30 seconds, then pour in slow circles until the scale reads 320 g. Let the brewer finish draining.

tabs.title: French press
tabs.subtitle: 30 g coffee / 480 g water
tabs.content: Add coarse-ground coffee and hot water, then give the grounds a stir. Steep for four minutes. Press gently and pour the coffee into cups or a separate jug to stop extraction.

tabs.title: AeroPress
tabs.subtitle: 15 g coffee / 220 g water
tabs.content_title: One cup in a few minutes
tabs.content: Rinse the paper filter and place the brewer on a sturdy mug. Add medium-fine coffee and hot water, stir, and insert the plunger slightly to hold the brew. After about two minutes, press gently.

settings.title: Adjust by taste
settings.description: Make the next cup with one small change and see if it moves in the direction you want.

items.title: Sharp or sour
items.description: Try a slightly finer grind so water can extract more flavor. Keep the weight of the coffee and water the same.

items.title: Dry or bitter
items.description: Try a slightly coarser grind. For pour-over, check whether water is taking much longer to drain than usual.

items.title: Weak but balanced
items.description: Use a little more coffee at the same water weight. Change one thing at a time so you can taste the difference.

settings.title: Keep the beans fresh
settings.description: Close the bag tightly after each use and keep it in a cool, dark cupboard.

tabs.tab_title: Should I grind the whole bag?
tabs.tab_content: Grind only what you need for each brew if you have a grinder. For pre-ground coffee, close the bag carefully and choose a smaller bag you can finish promptly.

tabs.tab_title: Can I freeze a spare bag?
tabs.tab_content: Freeze an airtight portion. Let the sealed portion warm to room temperature before opening to keep condensation away from the beans.

tabs.tab_title: What should I write on the bag?
tabs.tab_content: Record the roast date if available and the day you opened the bag. Keep a short note of your favorite recipe beside it.
